locator: Table 1 / AI Self-improvement / Capability threshold / Critical
context_stem: Tracked Category: AI Self-improvement — Capability threshold that could lead to the risk — Critical
excerpt: The model is capable of recursively self improving (i.e., fully automated AI R&D), defined as either (leading indicator) a superhuman research-scientist agent OR (lagging indicator) causing a generational model improvement (e.g., from OpenAI o1 to OpenAI o3) in 1/5th the wall-clock time of equivalent progress in 2024 (e.g., sped up to just 4 weeks) sustainably for several months.
paraphrase: Critical threshold: fully automated recursive self-improvement, indicated either by a superhuman research-scientist agent, or generational model improvement achieved in one-fifth the 2024 timeframe (about 4 weeks) sustained for several months.
stated_bar: 1/5th the wall-clock time of equivalent progress in 2024 (e.g., sped up to just 4 weeks)

locator: Table 1 / AI Self-improvement / Associated risk / Critical / part 1
context_stem: Tracked Category: AI Self-improvement — Associated risk of severe harm — Critical
excerpt: A major acceleration in the rate of AI R&D could rapidly increase the rate at which new capabilities and risks emerge, to the point where our current oversight practices are insufficient to identify and mitigate new risks,
paraphrase: A major R&D acceleration could outpace current oversight practices' ability to identify and mitigate new risks.

locator: Table 1 / AI Self-improvement / Associated risk / Critical / part 2
context_stem: Tracked Category: AI Self-improvement — Associated risk of severe harm — Critical
excerpt: including risks to maintaining human control of the AI system itself.
paraphrase: This includes risks to maintaining human control over the AI system.

locator: Table 1 / AI Self-improvement / Safeguard guidelines / Critical
context_stem: Tracked Category: AI Self-improvement — Risk-specific safeguard guidelines — Critical
excerpt: Until we have specified safeguards and security controls that would meet a Critical standard, halt further development
paraphrase: Development halts until safeguards and security controls meeting the Critical standard are specified.

excerpt: There are also some areas of frontier capability that do not meet the criteria to be Tracked Categories, but where we believe work is required now in order to prepare to effectively address risks of severe harms in the future.
paraphrase: Some capability areas don't meet Tracked Category criteria but warrant present preparatory work for future severe harm risks.

excerpt: These capabilities either need more research and threat modeling before they can be rigorously measured, or do not cause direct risks themselves but may need to be monitored because further advancement in this capability could undermine the safeguards we rely on to mitigate existing Tracked Category risks.
paraphrase: These capabilities either need more research before measurement, or don't cause direct risk themselves but could undermine safeguards for existing Tracked Categories.

excerpt: We call these Research Categories, and in these areas we will take the following steps, both internally and in collaboration with external experts:
paraphrase: These are called Research Categories, addressed through steps taken internally and with external experts.

context_stem: In these areas we will take the following steps, both internally and in collaboration with external experts:
excerpt: Further developing the threat models for the area,
paraphrase: Continue developing threat models for the research area.

context_stem: In these areas we will take the following steps, both internally and in collaboration with external experts:
excerpt: Advancing the science of capability measurement in the area and investing towards the development of rigorous evaluations (which could be achieved internally or via partnerships), and
paraphrase: Advance capability measurement science and invest in rigorous evaluations, internally or via partnerships.

context_stem: In these areas we will take the following steps, both internally and in collaboration with external experts:
excerpt: Sharing summaries of our findings with the public where feasible.
paraphrase: Share summaries of findings publicly where feasible.

excerpt: We will periodically review the latest research and findings for each Research Category.
paraphrase: Latest research and findings for each Research Category will be periodically reviewed.

excerpt: SAG will receive the results of such reviews and evaluate whether there is sufficient evidence to recommend updates to our internal practices or to the Preparedness Framework.
paraphrase: SAG receives review results and evaluates whether updates to internal practices or the Framework are warranted.

excerpt: ability for a model to execute a long-horizon sequence of actions sufficient to realize a “High” threat model (e.g., a cyberattack) without being directed by a human (including successful social engineering attacks when needed)
paraphrase: Long-range Autonomy is defined as the ability to execute long-horizon action sequences realizing a High threat model without human direction, including social engineering.

locator: Table 2 / Long-range Autonomy / Potential response / part 1
context_stem: Research Category: Long-range Autonomy — Potential response
excerpt: If a model has High or Critical capabilities in any of the Tracked Categories, require a “misalignment” safeguards report (see Section 4.2).
paraphrase: Models with High or Critical capability in any Tracked Category require a misalignment safeguards report.

locator: Table 2 / Long-range Autonomy / Potential response / part 2
context_stem: Research Category: Long-range Autonomy — Potential response
excerpt: As this category matures, we will make decisions about how this should influence our governance, including setting internal and external deployment safeguards milestones.
paraphrase: As Long-range Autonomy matures, decisions about its governance influence, including deployment safeguard milestones, will follow.
